$comment: Variant module: RESEARCH_REPORT. Byline: Claude Code · Opus 5 · 2026-08-29 12:59 EDT. Parent registry: ../document-markdown-v1.json. Emits no artifact — chunk pass only.

pass_chunk.strategy: one chunk per lowest-level heading section
pass_chunk.never_split: a markdown table — every row of a table stays in one chunk
pass_chunk.heading_path_note: Carry the full ancestor path (e.g. Part I > Threshold Hurdles > 1.1.2 Authentication) so a retrieved section is locatable without the surrounding document.
pass_chunk.rationale: Register R33 — a material finding must open to its exact source location with enough surrounding context to judge meaning. A heading section is that unit.
pass_chunk.measured_baseline: Current production chunking (RecursiveChunker character/1500) produces 46 chunks with 1 of 26 starting at a heading — section structure is destroyed. This variant exists to fix that.

artifact_rationale: Reference and authority material about the law, not case events. It is cited, not chronicled. No timeline rows.

known_content_hazards.tables: 14 table rows measured. A character-window chunker splits tables mid-body, making them unreadable and uncitable. Table integrity is a hard requirement here, not a nicety.
known_content_hazards.citation_spans: 50 legal citations. Splitting mid-citation breaks both retrieval and any downstream citation validation.
known_content_hazards.long_sections: Some sections exceed a typical chunk_size. Sub-splitting within a section is permitted, but every sub-chunk must retain the heading path.

open_questions: Chonkie TableChunker (candidate D) is a plausible complement for the tabular passages but was not measured — include it when the bake-off is completed.
Whether a section exceeding chunk_size sub-splits on paragraphs or on sentences.
